substeps.caption: Melt held at ~800 °C, O₂ at 45 ppm. The pour goes in this order, quickly: vibration ON, draining pressure, sealing rod UP, turbo as needed.
Vibration ON. Amplitude is a percentage of generator current: start about 90 % and adjust; lower gives finer powder but may stop atomizing.
Draining pressure: furnace above chamber pushes the melt out. Only the difference matters.
Sealing rod UP: the melt stream falls onto the plate. The first drops usually bounce off: a cold, dry plate does not wet.
A short TURBO push (1.5 bar) heats the plate and clears debris; pouring more at the start is what makes the plate wet.
Once the plate is hot every drop atomizes: droplets fly off the plate, freeze in the argon and fall to the cone. The stream lands mid-plate, beside the upper sonotrode, never on it.
The powder runs down the cone into the container. Too thin a stream gathers and drips; melt shooting past the plate means the pressure is too high (the Oct 2 lesson).
Two to three minutes of attention: amplitude slider, turbo pulses, plate position, with the operator at the window the whole time.
The crucible runs empty: next, the end-of-pour sequence (step 6).
